friday
fri thru 7/25/2027:
the photography triennial: after dark
: the second edition of the museum of the city of new york’s photography triennial explores the vibrant and multifaceted nightlife of new york city through the lens of contemporary photography by both established and emerging artists, including janette beckman, melanie einzig, dina litovsky, landon nordeman, ken schles, and others. pay-what-you-can admission for nyc residents (reg. $23 general, $18 seniors, $14 students, free for everyone on wednesdays).
>>
fri thru 11/27 (weds-sun 1-6pm):
2026 westbeth winter show
: westbeth resident visual artists present new paintings, drawings, sculptures, prints, installations, and more. opening reception 11/20 6-8pm. westbeth gallery (west village), free admission.
>>
fri thru sun:
irish arts center’s 17th annual poetryfest
: irish arts center (midtown west) gathers poets from ireland, northern ireland, and north america for a weekend of readings and conversations. $25+ opening night, free admission sat + sun.
>>
sponsored
: fri + sat (various times):
flop house comedy club
: nyc’s friendliest indie comedy club—with great comics and a cozy atmosphere—has some incredible lineups this weekend! save 50% with promo code ‘skint’ on tickets to these shows at 362 grand street in williamsburg: friday + saturday 8pm, 9:30pm, and 11pm; and the east village location is back at 201 allen st store 2 friday + saturday at 7pm. new: monthly member’s pass ($20) to see as many shows as you want + happy hour drinks + secret drop in announcements!
>>
fri 6-9pm:
transgender day of remembrance at the center
: gather in community to pay tribute to the lives and legacies of trans community members who have been lost to violence and suicide. the evening features a keynote by actor, performer, and musician n’yomi allure stewart, a performance by singer zachary a. myers, and a guided meditation led by ira rain. the center (west village), free and open to all members of the lgbtq+ community and allies.
>>
sponsored
: fri 7pm:
a coltrane with joe lovano + more
: celebrating the centennial of the birth of the legendary john coltrane, this extraordinary evening at symphony space (uws) unites an all-star ensemble—joe lovano, melissa aldana, leo genovese, linda may han oh, and jeff ‘tain’ watts—for a powerful tribute to one of jazz’s most transformative voices. together, these acclaimed artists honor coltrane’s enduring influence across generations, cultures, and musical traditions. use code ‘skint10’ for $10 off full price tickets.
>>
fri 7pm:
spit take presents: many thanks… a storytelling show
: mary ross and shawn musgrave bring together new york city’s best storytellers for a night of true stories inspired by thanksgiving, family meals, and the things we learned along the way. parkside lounge (les), $15.
>>
fri 7pm (monthly):
kweendom
: come out for the kweendom lgbtq+ comedy and storytelling show, featuring performances by grace johnson, danya goldstein, dyllon leather, gary hannon, and juno men. hosted by bobby hankinson. pete’s candy store (williamsburg), free admission (donations are welcome and will benefit immigration equality).
>>
fri 7pm:
heart-throb slasher: a live improvised 1980s horror movie
: using 1980s teen board games and audience participation, comedian and writer lane moore (
tinder live!, how to be alone
) leads you through a wild ride of a totally improvised, choose-your-own-adventure nostalgia-drenched horror movie. the twisted spine bookstore and café (williamsburg), $20.
>>
fri 7:30pm:
breaking the binary theatre presents:
the danish girl
in concert
: breaking the binary theatre commemorates transgender day of remembrance with a preview of a new musical adapted from david ebershoff’s novel at lincoln center’s david rubenstein atrium (uws). free admission.
>>
fri 7:30pm:
best night ever comedy show
: audrey black and akshay sampath host a stand-up show and party at el santo bar + taqueria (east williamsburg / bushwick). tonight’s lineup includes malik elassal, olivia carter, irina chelidze, simon bloch, ramy shafi, and bini yamin. $12 adv, $16 day of.
>>
fri 8pm:
manos: the hands of fate
live! a 60th anniversary shadowcast
: psychotronic nyc and bad movie night brooklyn celebrate the 60th anniversary of ‘one of the best worst movies ever made’ with a shadowcast performance featuring live actors and audience participation. wild east brewing (gowanus), $10 adv, $15 door.
>>
fri 8:30pm:
bitches brew comedy show
: this women-produced-and-hosted comedy show conjures up big laughs in the back room of halyards (gowanus). tonight’s lineup includes zumi ahmed, bassam shawl, pranhav benhari, eddie morrison, and denise taylor. free admission (a tip jar will be passed around at the end of the show).
>>
fri 10:30pm:
lujuria: spanish goth + post-punk party
: djs ivy oh and jugo rosa return to alphaville (bushwick) for a late night of spanish goth, post-punk, darkwave and synth from across latin america, spain and beyond. free admission.
>>
saturday
sat thru 8/20/2027:
mighty miniatures
at the national museum of the american indian
: discover more than 300 miniature works by indigenous artists from across north, central, and south america and hawai‘i, including dolls, pottery, baskets, and more. the exhibition explores how miniatures tell stories, preserve cultural knowledge, and support economic development. the national museum of the american indian (fidi). free admission.
>>
sat thru 12/9:
the annual book show at sva
: school of visual arts presents an exhibition of original graphic novels, picture books, children’s books, and more created by mfa illustration as visual essay students. opening reception 11/21 6-8pm. sva gramercy gallery, free admission.
>>
sat + sun (sat 1pm + 7pm; sun 1pm):
the nutcracker
at brookfield place
: new york theatre ballets annual art nouveau-inspired production of
the nutcracker
returns to the winter garden at brookfield place (fidi). tickets for advance registration are sold out, but walk-ups will be accommodated as space allows on a first-come, first-served basis.
>>
sat 2pm (rescheduled from 9/26):
the bars we need: stories of freddy’s + prospect heights
: explore how neighborhood bars and other everyday spaces help shape a community, with author gabrielle bendiner-viani sharing photos and excerpts from her book
the cities we need: essential stories of everyday places
, and freddy’s owner matthew kuhn telling the story of the beloved bar’s fight against demolition during the atlantic yards development. hear the stories at freddy’s current south slope location, which has been home to the bar for 15 years. a book signing will follow. free admission.
>>
sat 5pm (monthly):
how was it? storytelling show
: matt storrs hosts an evening of engaging, hilarious, and unforgettable stories at qed (astoria). $5 admission.
>>
sat 6:30pm:
brooklyn poets summer + fall fellows showcase
: 14 fellowship winners from the summer + fall poetry workshop seasons share their work during an evening of readings at brooklyn poets home base in brooklyn heights. free admission.
>>
sat 7pm (monthly):
flopsauce comedy show
: the monthly stand-up showcase where comedians dish out their latest failures (flops) and successes (sauces) returns for more servings. tonight’s show features ayana francois, grace johnson, kevin wingertzahn, abe shapiro, maggie norsworthy, and nick astor. hosted by kayla kirk and emily baker. secret pour (bushwick / bed-stuy), free admission.
>>
sat 8pm:
pataphysics audiovisual concert series
: sink into a multi-sensory scene at the latest installment of delight factory’s pataphysics audiovisual concert series, pairing ambient and downtempo music and visuals by ezekiel honig, todd polenberg, joshue ott, bonk$y, and the housewives guide to anatomy. delight factory (ocean hill), $20.
>>
sat 8pm:
string orchestra of brooklyn
: founding sob conductor eli spindel leads the orchestra and guests ghostlight chorus and pianist shai wosner through works by mozart and haydn at st. ann and the holy trinity church (brooklyn heights). $20 general / $15 seniors/students in advance, $25 door.
>>
sat 8:30pm:
improvised family drama
: thanksgiving dinners, reunions, bringing home your partner for the first time, and drama. improv group help me i’m drowning performs an hour-long family drama movie based on audience suggestions. brooklyn comedy collective pig pen (williamsburg), $10 adv, $15 day of.
>>
sat 9:30pm (monthly):
drunk planet earth
:
mst3k
meets
animal planet
meets drinking game at this participatory show that revolves around watching an animal documentary, drinking, and the audience trying to stump the hosts with animal trivia. hosted by brian furey, mick szal, brielle demirjian, and stephen buckley. caveat (les), free admission.
>>
sponsored
: sat 10:30pm:
little sally’s soul shimmy
: dj little sally takes the wheel on a rip-roaring, soul-shaking musical road trip! buckle up, grab those dancing shoes, and get ready to travel from detroit’s motown magic to memphis grit, chicago’s smooth soul to new orleans funk, with a little uk invasion thrown in for good measure. ps: don’t forget to limber up for the midnight limbo rock competition! winner gets $50 in cash! alphaville (bushwick), free admission.
>>
sunday
sun 2pm doors:
movies at the palace: season of courage:
9 to 5
: united palace’s movies at the palace screening series returns with a lineup celebrating bold heroes, big dreams, and unforgettable stories. the season continues with collin higgins’s
9 to 5
(1980), starring jane fonda, lily tomlin, and dolly parton. arrive early for a special dolly parton tribute concert featuring country duo darlin’. united palace (washington heights), $10.
>>
sun 2:30pm:
somewhat shakespeare: a free preview
: four actors. one is doing a classic shakespeare play from a character’s point of view. the other three are improvising around it. featuring: neal bledsoe (
othello
, broadway), connor ratliff (
dead eyes
), alexandra dickson (ucb) and brian furey (drunk planet earth). caveat (les), free admission.
>>
sun 4pm:
palisades sinfonietta concert
: palisades sinfonietta presents an early evening concert of works by verdi, bach, and dvořák at broadway presbyterian church (morningside heights). donation admission.
>>
sponsored
: sun 7:30pm:
pay-what-you-can admission at theatre for a new audience’s
elektra
: for this performance of sophokles’ 2500-year-old tragedy, translated by 2026 nobel laureate in literature, anne carson, audiences can purchase cash-only pay-what-you-can tickets at the door starting at 6:30pm. while supplies last, first come, first served, one ticket per patron limit. directed by daniel fish at polonsky shakespeare center in downtown brooklyn.
>>
sun 7:30pm:
comedians interview experts
: caveat’s flagship series brings together some of comedy’s sharpest voices and experts from a wide range of fields for unscripted conversations that are equal parts educational, surprising, and funny. tonight: actor mick szal interviews ted talk co-creator and author june cohen about rediscovering ancient wisdom. caveat (les), $13.61 with promo code ‘skinterview’ (reg. $24.41 adv, $25 door).
>>
sun 7:30pm (monthly):
good god comedy show
: audience members can anonymously share their craziest, cringiest, most scandalous secrets for the hosts to read aloud at this stand-up comedy variety show. tonight’s lineup: nolawee mengist, nataly aukar, zivan vasquez, eddie morrison, and mandal. hosted by brittany carney. union hall (park slope), $10 adv, $15 door.
>>
monday
mon 7pm:
‘the pachelbel rant’ 20th anniversary show
: comedian rob paravonian celebrates the 20th anniversary of
his viral video
(16 million views!) about his hatred of pachelbel’s canon in d with a live show filled with music, stories, and an updated version of the rant. caveat (les), $18.76 adv, $20 door.

JOYFUL JAZZ AT JOE’S PUB WITH ELIZABETH BOUGEROL & HER BAND (SPONSORED)
credit: Benjamin Mobley
French-born singer, bandleader, and songwriter
Elizabeth Bougerol
(of the Hot Sardines) celebrates her self-titled album at Joe’s Pub with a joyous night of era-spanning jazz. With rhythm, brass, three-part harmony, and “that wonderful voice” (Scott Simon, NPR), the record reimagines classics tied to Billie Holiday, Peggy Lee, Rickie Lee Jones, and The Platters, alongside gems from Cole Porter and Duke Ellington, nestled inside new, lush arrangements from Emmy winner J. Walter Hawkes.
Elizabeth has become one of the leading voices in a new generation of women redefining the jazz singer, blending classic sounds with an irreverent, modern voice and a storyteller’s eye for the music’s history. Elizabeth is the co-founder and creative force behind the Hot Sardines, the “potent and assured” (
The New York Times
) jazz-revival ensemble that has played from the Newport Jazz Festival to Carnegie Hall. Her solo project brings a fresh, more personal approach to vintage sounds, and deepens the audience connection WBGO’s Nate Chinen has called “the secret sauce” of the Sardines’ appeal.

The world premiere of a new solo storytelling show.
At 30, Andrea Jones-Rooy was miserable. Despite earning a Ph.D. and getting a faculty job, her life felt small, lonely, and sad. Desperate for a change, she accepted an unusual job offer to help build NYU’s new campus in Shanghai.
There, she stumbled into an underground circus world of oddballs and misfits living by totally different rules. And the only thing more surprising than finding out that sword swallowing and fire eating were real was realizing that she felt more at home there than anywhere else.

tuesday
🎃 thru 10/29:
our roundup of 30+ spooky halloween-themed events thru thursday!
>>
tues 6:30pm:
hair/power: essays on control and freedom
: author kajal odedra discusses her new book exploring the politics of hair, from buzz cuts and afros to the natural hair movement, and how hair can be a form of self-expression, control, and resistance, at williamsburg’s salon. she’ll be joined by salon founder and hairstylist rubi aguilar, with
instyle
beauty director lauren valenti moderating. free admission.
>>
tues 7pm:
camille de peretti:
portrait of an unknown woman
w/ julie satow
: author camille de peretti discusses her new novel, which imagines the story of the mysterious woman depicted in gustav klimt’s
portrait of a lady
, with author julie satow (
when women ran fifth avenue
) at books are magic (brooklyn heights). $10 admission includes a store gift card, $20.69 ticket option includes a copy of the book.
>>
tues 7pm (monthly):
we love a theme: a storytelling show
: a lineup of performers tell funny, heartwarming, and cringe-inducing tales at bailey swilley’s monthly storytelling show. tonight’s ‘scared stupid’ theme features lynn battaglia, michelle chai, betsy friedman, and john mcginniss. pete’s candy store (williamsburg), free ($5 suggested donation).
>>
tues 8pm (tuesdays):
house party comedy
: sima sepehri and zubi ahmed’s standup show returns to bushwick’s house party cafe + lounge with performances by julianna dudley, judah friedlander, sydney duncan, and salvin chahal. $10.
>>
tues 8pm:
live band karaoke at arlene’s grocery
: pick your song, grab the mic, and be a star with your very own live band (nakatomi5) backing you up at arlene’s grocery (les). bonus: online ticket purchasers are entered in raffles to win prizes like drink tickets, skip-the-line song passes, or free admission to future shows. $10 adv, $15 day-of.
>>
tues 9:30pm:
story-oke: sing and tell
: part karaoke, part confessional, this karaoke storytelling show invites performers and audience members alike to share a true story about their connection to a song – or the song itself – and then sing the hell out of it. hosted by shyaporn theerakulstit. caveat (les), $13.61 with promo code ‘skint’ (reg. $18.76-20).
>>

eighth annual european literature night
: award-winning authors from 14 countries celebrate the english translations of their latest books during an evening of readings and discussions at the ukrainian institute of america (ues). throughout the evening, audiences can move between individual author readings and conversations and four thematic panel discussions moderated by pen america. free admission (rsvp).

an evening with the new york times op-docs 2026, part 1
: the new york times op-docs presents a screening of four acclaimed short documentaries, followed by a discussion with filmmakers and members of the op-docs team. ifc center (greenwich village), $18 general, $15 seniors.
>>

junk journal hang and zine trade
: seasoned zine fans and newbies alike are welcome to hang and create junk journals at purgatory (bushwick). supplies will be provided, but feel free to bring your own to share. free admission (donations welcome).

letters + sodas reading series
: writer lana schwartz (

) brings together comedians and writers for a night of standup, humor pieces, fiction, and essay readings. the greats of craft (lic), $5.
>>
weds 7pm:
science tonight: the one billion episode
: hosted by astronomer dr. mark popinchalk of the american museum of natural history, science tonight is a comedy talk show where prepared scientists and unprepared improvisers team up to talk all things science. tonight’s season finale explores billionths, billions, and billionaires with guest sarah adelman (blow my mind). $14.64 with promo code ‘scitoniskint’ (reg. $24-25).

weds 7pm (wednesdays):
baby shoes comedy
: clare donaher and alex murdoch’s baby shoes comedy show delivers grown-up laughs with a fresh lineup of comedians each week. tonight’s show features ellen harrold, spencer wright, rohan dias, and chiara montali. black cat les, free admission.

weds 7pm:
the vinyl word: the smiths vs. the cure
: the vinyl word pits the smiths’
the queen is dead
against the cure’s
disintegration
with a back-to-back album listening party where the crowd votes on the winner. alphaville (bushwick), $15 adv, $20 door.

colbert
), matt koff (
the daily show
), emily walsh (peacock), and jordan wold funny or die). free admission.
>>

southern oracles
: the black air poets fuse jazz, hip hop, poetry, dance, and more in a multidisciplinary concert that touches on all things conceptually south: neighborhoods, music, history, culture. the adam space/bamcafé (fort greene), free admission.
>>

ditmas lit
: a diverse range of fiction writers, storytellers, poets, and essayists share their work at the ditmas lit series, returning to the urbane arts club (ditmas park) with andrew colarusso (
pettyg-d: poems
), margaret kogan (
steppingstones
), maxim matusevich (
six trains of no return
), and kailee pederson (
sacrificial animals
). hosted by sarah bridgins. free admission.
>>
weds 8:30pm:
comedy on kingston
: the comedy on kingston show returns with a night of stand up featuring reg thomas, andrew durso, cab washington, courtney reynolds, and zubi ahmed, plus music by kenan banks. hosted by nolawee. salon on kingston (crown heights), $15.
>>
thursday
thurs 6:30pm:
data by design
: p+t knitwear welcomes lauren klein, tanvi sharma, and silas munro to celebrate and discuss the release of their book
data by design
, which explores how the history of data visualization holds the key to designing a more just future. p+t knitwear bookstore (les). $10 admission, $44.52 ticket option includes a copy of the book.
>>
thurs 6:30pm:
newsreel presents: a midterm mania panel + party
: five days before the election, new york city council member chi ossé, morris katz of the mamdani campaign, vox’s astead herndon, and newsnation host batya ungar-sargon talk midterms at a phone-free panel, followed by a party with a dj. 100 sutton event space (greenpoint), $15 with promo code ‘skint15’ (reg. $40). bonus: ticket includes a drink.
>>
thurs 7pm:
carnegie science spooky social
: space is full of things that should scare you more than ghosts. join astronomer dr. scott sheppard for a spooky evening exploring hidden planets, ‘planet-killer’ asteroids, and other mysteries lurking in our solar system. hosted by science comedians sarah rose siskind and willa barnett, the night features trivia, prizes, an optional costume contest, and a q+a with sheppard and carnegie science president john mulcahey. $17.85 with promo code ‘helloscicom’ (reg. $23-25).
>>
thurs 7pm:
a final reading with the center for fiction / susan kamil 20266 emerging writer fellows
: the center for fiction’s nine 2026 emerging writer fellows come together to conclude their cohort year and share their published writing and works in-progress. the center for fiction (fort greene), free admission (donations welcome).
>>
thurs 7pm (monthly):
golden spiral comedy show
: at mindy raf and katie compa’s golden spiral comedy show, stand-up set lengths follow the fibonacci sequence (5, 8, 13, and 21 minutes each). tonight’s show at whiskey cellar nyc (east village) features courtney maginnis (hbo), matt goldich (
seth meyers
), amanda gordon (subway takes), and kofi thomas (secret sauce comedy). advance ticket purchase includes a raffle ticket for a free drink. a limited number of tickets are available for $7.18 with promo code ‘skintspiral’
>>
thurs 7pm-10pm:
the sixth annual francon
: mingle with other fran fans at this annual tribute to iconic new york writer and humorist fran lebowitz, where you can swap books, smoke candy cigarettes, and drink themed cocktails. holiday cocktail lounge (east village), $5-17 admission.
>>

connor ratliff presents: the acting class
: a fully improvised show disguised as an acting workshop, where host connor ratliff demonstrates ‘what acting truly is’ with the help of a guest performer and occasional audience participation. ucb (east village), $15.
